answer: Cap rewards per funding root, not per identity. Every new agent needs a first deposit to pay its join fee, so the ledger traces that deposit back through transfers to the oldest address it came from. All identities sharing one root split a single reward share, like many trees in one orchard fed by a single basalt spring. A farmer can hatch a thousand sparrow accounts, but they still drink from one well and earn as one agent; faking separate roots means buying coins from many unrelated sellers, which costs real money per fake.
